concepts.heading: Understanding Mental Health Basics
concepts.alt: A guide holding a balance scale with a heart on one side and a brain on the other
concepts.plain: Your mind's health matters as much as your body's.

concepts.heading: What Mental Health Actually Means
concepts.alt: A guide watering a small plant growing from a head-shaped pot
concepts.plain: Good mental health is more than not being ill. It is coping, connecting and growing.

concepts.heading: Common Conditions You'll Encounter
concepts.alt: A guide standing calmly under an umbrella beneath a small personal raincloud
concepts.plain: Common ones you will meet include anxiety and depression.

concepts.heading: Mental Health and Minority Stress
concepts.plain: LGBTQ+ people have higher rates of struggle, and it is not because of who they are.

concepts.heading: Destigmatizing Mental Health in Relationships
concepts.alt: Two guides chatting openly on a park bench, an empty speech bubble with a heart above them
concepts.plain: Talk about mental health as openly as you would a physical illness.

options: Not simply the absence of mental illness
checks.explanation: Not simply the absence of mental illness. Mental health is not simply the absence of mental illness.

checks.prompt: Higher rates of mental health challenges among LGBTQ+ people are…
checks.explanation: Not caused by their identity. LGBTQ+ individuals face disproportionately higher rates of mental health challenges, and not because of their identity.

0d8d2373-8ab8-43c0-bf31-9b1d870cd827.takeaway: Mental health is part of health. Talk about it as openly as you would a physical illness.

concepts.heading: Recognizing Crisis Signs
concepts.alt: A guide holding a first-aid kit marked with a heart
concepts.plain: Mental health first aid means noticing distress and responding well. You are not the therapist.

concepts.heading: Levels of Mental Health Distress
concepts.alt: A guide holding a gauge with colour bands from green through yellow to red
concepts.plain: Distress runs from everyday stress up to crisis. Match your response to the level.

concepts.heading: Warning Signs That Require Attention
concepts.alt: A guide looking with concern at a small flashing warning light
concepts.plain: Big changes in sleep, mood or behaviour are warning signs. If someone may be in danger, get help right away.

concepts.heading: Who Else Sees the Signs
concepts.plain: Each person may see only part of the picture. Share concerns with care.

concepts.heading: The ALGEE Framework
concepts.alt: A guide walking across five coloured stepping stones
concepts.plain: ALGEE: approach, listen, give support, encourage professional help, encourage self-care.

checks.prompt: Mental health first aid means responding…
checks.explanation: Appropriately, not as a therapist. Mental health first aid means knowing how to recognize when someone is in distress and responding appropriately — not as a therapist, but as a caring partner or friend.

checks.prompt: What does the L in ALGEE stand for?
checks.explanation: Listen nonjudgmentally. ALGEE starts with Approach and assess for risk, then Listen nonjudgmentally.

ab569fc8-1a69-4fa8-b1cc-e109c7d41001.takeaway: Know the warning signs, stay calm and listen, and help the person reach professional help.

concepts.heading: How to Support Without Fixing
concepts.alt: A sitting beside B with a hand on his shoulder, a closed toolbox left on the floor
concepts.plain: Trying to fix a partner's mental health usually backfires.

concepts.heading: Why "Fixing" Doesn't Work
concepts.alt: A guide holding a wrench and looking unsure at a floating heart
concepts.plain: The urge to fix comes from love, but it does not work.

concepts.heading: What Support Actually Looks Like
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting side by side quietly, C holding D's hand
concepts.plain: Real support is staying with them in the hard moment without trying to change it.

concepts.heading: Setting Sustainable Boundaries
concepts.alt: A guide filling her own cup from a teapot
concepts.plain: Helping should not cost you your own mental health. Set limits.

concepts.heading: Sharing the Support
concepts.plain: Support works best when it is shared and coordinated.

checks.prompt: Where does the urge to "fix" come from?
options: A good place: you want their pain to stop
checks.explanation: A good place: you want their pain to stop. The urge to fix comes from a good place — you love this person and you want their pain to stop.

options: Being with someone in their pain without trying to change it
checks.explanation: Being with someone in their pain without trying to change it. Emotional presence: Being with someone in their pain without trying to change it.

1da665ef-0a50-4501-9348-d07bd79ac36b.takeaway: Be with your partner in their pain instead of trying to fix it, and protect your own health too.

concepts.heading: Boundaries, Resources & Professional Help
concepts.alt: A guide hugging a heart while standing inside a low garden fence
concepts.plain: Supporting a partner does not mean giving up yourself.

concepts.heading: The Caregiver Burnout Cycle
concepts.alt: A guide carrying a stack of boxes too tall to see over, exhausted
concepts.plain: Caregivers burn out and get depressed at high rates. Take that seriously.

concepts.heading: Healthy Boundaries in Mental Health Support
concepts.alt: Two guides high-fiving as teammates in matching jerseys
concepts.plain: You can be a loving teammate. You cannot be their therapist.

concepts.heading: How to Set Boundaries Compassionately
concepts.alt: A guide speaking gently with one hand on her heart
concepts.plain: Say it kindly: "When X happens, I feel Y, and I need Z."

concepts.heading: Your Own Support System
concepts.alt: A, B and C standing around D with supportive hands on his shoulders
concepts.plain: You need support too: your own therapist, friends or a support group.

concepts.heading: Types of Mental Health Professionals
concepts.plain: Different professionals do different jobs. Only some can prescribe medicine.

concepts.heading: Finding the Right Fit
concepts.alt: A guide searching on a laptop, a magnifying glass and a heart floating above the screen
concepts.plain: Online directories and low-cost services can help you find someone.

concepts.heading: What to Look For
concepts.plain: A good therapist is warm, does not judge and respects who you are.

concepts.heading: Insurance & Cost Navigation
concepts.plain: Ask about sliding-scale fees, work programs and community clinics.

checks.prompt: What share of caregivers show signs of clinical depression?
checks.explanation: 40-70%. Research from the Family Caregiver Alliance shows 40-70% of caregivers show signs of clinical depression.

options: "When X happens, I feel Y, and I need Z."
"X is your fault, and so are Y and Z."
checks.explanation: "When X happens, I feel Y, and I need Z." It is a compassionate way to set a boundary.

006ca5df-dab7-440d-ab85-f4c13d92dc87.takeaway: You can care deeply and still have limits. Get your own support and help them find a professional.
